title: Real Estate Investing: Taxing REITs, Funds & Property
description: Investing in real estate can be done directly through physical property, or indirectly via REITs or REIT mutual funds. Capital gains tax rules differ signific.

faq.q: What is the main tax advantage of REITs over physical property?
faq.a: REITs typically have a shorter holding period of 24 months for long-term capital gains, compared to 36 months for physical property.

faq.q: Are REIT mutual funds taxed differently from direct REITs?
faq.a: Yes, REIT mutual funds are generally treated as debt funds for tax purposes, meaning LTCG applies after 36 months with indexation, unlike direct REITs which have a 24-month LTCG period and 10% tax without indexation (on gains over ₹1 lakh).

faq.q: Is TDS applicable on income distributions from REITs?
faq.a: Yes, certain components of REIT distributions, such as interest and rental income, are subject to TDS, typically at 10% for resident unitholders.

faq.q: Can I claim indexation benefit on REIT capital gains?
faq.a: No, long-term capital gains from direct REIT units (held over 24 months) are taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh, without indexation benefit.

faq.q: How is rental income from physical property taxed?
faq.a: Rental income is taxed under "Income from House Property," allowing for a 30% standard deduction and deductions for home loan interest.

faq.q: What happens if a REIT mutual fund distributes dividends (IDCW)?
faq.a: IDCW payouts from REIT mutual funds are generally added to your income and taxed at your applicable slab rate, similar to debt fund dividends.

based_on.title: REITs vs REIT mutual funds vs physical property: A complete guide to capital gains tax, TDS and post-tax returns
